facts.text: Commentators disagree about whether a trained-then-frozen machine-learning detector is "self-evolving" under Annex I Part A of EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 and therefore triggers notified-body assessment; some interpret any machine-learning safety function as falling within scope.
facts.quote: Whether a trained-then-frozen machine-learning detector is "self-evolving"** under Annex I Part A of Regulation 2023/1230, which would trigger notified-body assessment. Commentators differ, and some read any machine-learning safety function as in scope.

facts.text: For the disputed classification of a trained-then-frozen machine-learning safety detector under Annex I Part A of EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230, a notified-body opinion should be obtained early.
facts.quote: A notified-body opinion should be obtained early [82, 85].

facts.text: Proponents of Bayesian priors derived from simulation report large reductions in physical testing, whereas critics emphasize sensitivity to prior strength; the conservative Bayesian road-testing analysis gives 69 million to 476 million miles depending on prior strength.
facts.quote: Proponents report large reductions in physical testing; critics note that the result is highly sensitive to the prior (69 million to 476 million miles depending on prior strength in the conservative Bayesian road-testing analysis) [37].

facts.text: Experts contest whether scenario-based validation or mileage- or exposure-based validation should be the primary safety argument; on-road regulators using NATM employ a multi-pillar mix, but the weighting is contested.
facts.quote: **Scenario-based against mileage- or exposure-based validation as the primary argument.** On-road regulators (NATM) use a multi-pillar mix; the weighting is contested [38, 42].

facts.text: Experts disagree about how aggressively rare-event acceleration can replace naturalistic exposure: importance sampling is sound when distributions are modelled accurately, but determining those distributions for open-ended safety-critical interactions is itself difficult.
facts.quote: Importance sampling is sound when the distributions are modelled accurately, but determining them for open-ended safety-critical interactions is itself hard

facts.text: In the debate over replacing naturalistic exposure with rare-event acceleration, strong acceleration demonstrated for a narrow on-road cut-in model cannot be extrapolated to a quarry containing workers, rocks, articulated machines, dust and changing terrain.
facts.quote: strong acceleration shown for a narrow on-road cut-in model cannot be extrapolated to a quarry with workers, rocks, articulated machines, dust and changing terrain [30, 34].

facts.text: Experts disagree less about whether synthetic data helps a safety claim than about how much real data must still support that claim; no defensible universal synthetic-to-real data ratio exists.
facts.quote: Experts disagree less about whether synthetic data helps than about the residual real-data requirement; no defensible universal synthetic-to-real ratio exists [54, 60].

facts.text: Experts disagree about whether generative world models can serve as validation tools or should serve only as training tools.
facts.quote: **Generative world models as a validation tool versus a training tool only.**
